answer.rationale: The single most load-bearing inherited claim for the tempting move (full switch to the low-cost vendor) is memory_c2 — it is the only evidence that this vendor can carry primary volume, and the archived record needs to show at what volume, what component criticality, and whether the line had buffer at the time. 'Onboarding was quick' at last year's volume is not evidence of a clean 14-day cutover at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer. I also want memory_c3, because dual-sourcing is my intended path and I need to know whether that success was on this same constrained component and whether qualification time was days or months; if qualification was slow, a second source cannot be stood up inside 14 days either. memory_c4 and memory_c6 are effectively dead this cycle: the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so the negotiate/multi-year levers those memories describe are unavailable regardless of how well they worked before, and I am treating them as ruled out by current facts rather than by evidence quality. memory_c5 (defer) is not usable because the contract does not auto-renew — deferring here is not a costless hold, it is a lapse into the shortage-exposed state. So: qualify the low-cost vendor on a guarded minority share of volume alongside continuity of incumbent supply, rather than betting the whole line on one archived data point. Downstream value risk: the 18% mandate is a cost signal that, taken as the sole objective, quietly converts into delivery risk that shows up on the line and not in the sourcing scorecard; a guarded second source may under-deliver the mandate this cycle and I would rather report a partial cost miss than an unrecoverable stockout at 94% utilization with no buffer. Uncertainty I am not resolving: whether the low-cost vendor's quoted price survives a real qualification audit, whether their quote assumes volumes they have never actually shipped us, and whether the incumbent's price refusal is final or a posture that changes once a qualified alternate exists. If the archive shows memory_c2 came from a comparable-volume, comparable-criticality switch with a fast ramp, I would move toward a larger allocation shift; if it came from a small or non-critical spend, I hold the guarded scale and accept missing part of the mandate.
